rot.convert.ideia.barreira.e1: Attack: now the whole game, from the centre to mate. The bishop is dark-squared: the mating net only works on a1 or h8. In the first five moves, the three pieces came together in the centre.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.e2: The plan has three stages: the barrier drives the black king to the edge; Delétang's triangles lead it to the corner of the bishop's colour; the final net gives mate. At every move, recognise the stage.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.e3: And there is a clock: if 50 moves pass with no capture and no pawn move, Black can claim a draw. That is the fifty-move rule. From this position, mate with best play takes 25 moves.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l1: Your king goes to c4 and covers b5, c5 and d5. With the bishop covering c7 and d6, the black king is left with only b6, b7 and d7.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l2: The black king goes to b6, towards a8: with a dark-squared bishop, a8 is not the corner of the bishop's colour, and mate cannot be forced there.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l3: The knight goes to b5, protected by your king, and covers a7 and c7, on the black king's way to a8.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l4: The black king goes to a6 and sticks to the edge, away from your king.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l5: The bishop goes to e3 and covers b6 and a7. The black king only has a5 and b7.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l6: The black king goes to b7, one square from a8.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l7: Your king goes to c5 and covers b6 and c6. The black king is left with a6, a8, b8 and c8, all on the a8 side.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l8: The black king goes to b8, on the edge, still next to a8.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l9: Your king goes to b6 and covers a7, b7 and c7. The black king only has a8 and c8.
rot.convert.ideia.barreira.l10: The black king steps into a8. The barrier ended on move 10: the king is in the corner, but in the light one, where mate cannot be forced.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.e1: Attack: move 11, and the stage changes: now come Delétang's triangles. The black king is on a8, the wrong corner, and must be led along the eighth rank to h8, the corner of the bishop's colour.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l1: Check on c7: the knight drives the black king out of a8. With your king on b6, it only has b8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l2: Forced: the black king goes to b8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l3: Your king goes to c6 and protects the knight. The knight covers a8, and the bishop a7: the black king only has c8, towards h8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l4: Forced: the black king goes to c8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l5: The bishop goes to a7 and closes b8: the black king cannot go back to the wrong corner and only has d8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l6: Forced: the black king goes to d8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l7: The knight goes to d5 and covers e7. The black king stays on the edge, with c8 and e8.
rot.convert.ideia.borda.l8: The black king goes to e8, away from your pieces, and eyes f7, the way back to the centre.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.e1: Attack: move 15, still in Delétang's triangles. The black king has left the wrong corner and is on e8; now the bishop returns to the centre to close its diagonals.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l1: The bishop goes to d4 and covers f6 and g7, on the black king's way to h8. It has d8, f7 and f8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l2: The black king goes to f7 and looks for a way to the centre through e6 or g6.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l3: The knight goes to f4 and closes e6 and g6; the bishop closes f6 and g7. The black king is left with e7, e8, f8 and g8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l4: The black king goes to e7, towards your king and away from h8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l5: Your king goes to c7 and closes d6, d7 and d8. The black king only has e8, f7 and f8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l6: The black king goes to e8, on the edge, away from the knight.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l7: The bishop goes to f2, heading for h4, to enter the diagonal from d8 to h4.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l8: The black king goes back to e7 and waits.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l9: Check on h4: the bishop enters the diagonal from d8 to h4 and closes f6. The black king only has e8, f7 and f8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l10: The black king goes to e8, the defence that delays mate the longest.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l11: The bishop goes to g5, on the same diagonal, and closes d8 and e7. The black king only has f7 and f8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l12: The black king goes to f7, close to the centre again.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l13: Your king goes to d6 and closes e6 and e7; the knight closes g6, and the bishop f6. The black king is left with e8, f8, g7 and g8.
rot.convert.ideia.triangulos.l14: The black king goes back to e8, away from h8. The triangle of d8, h8 and h4 is closed, with it inside.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.e1: Attack: move 22, and the bishop on g5 covers the diagonal from d8 to h4: with the eighth rank and the h-file, it closes Delétang's middle triangle, with the black king inside.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.e2: Under the fifty-move rule, Black could only claim a draw 29 moves from now; mate needs 9. What remains is to shrink the triangle and build the net.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l1: The bishop goes to e7, on the same diagonal, and closes d8 and f8. The black king only has f7.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l2: Forced: the black king goes to f7 and attacks the bishop, which your king protects.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l3: Your king goes to d7, keeps protecting the bishop and closes e8. The black king only has g7 and g8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l4: The black king goes to g8, next to h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l5: Your king goes to e8 and closes f7 and f8. The black king is left with g7, h7 and h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l6: The black king goes to g7 and threatens to go to h6, further from your king.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l7: The bishop returns to g5, on the same diagonal, and closes f6 and h6. The black king only has g8, h7 and h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l8: The black king goes back to g8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l9: The knight goes to e6 and closes g7 and f8. The black king only has h7 and h8: this is the final net.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l10: The black king goes to h7.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l11: Your king goes to f7 and closes g6, g7 and g8. The black king only has h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l12: Forced: the black king goes to h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l13: Waiting move: the bishop goes to c1 and still covers h6. Closing h7 now without check would leave the black king stalemated.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l14: Forced: the black king goes to h7.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l15: Check on f8: the knight, protected by your king, pushes the black king back to h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l16: Forced: the black king goes back to h8.
rot.convert.ideia.rede.l17: Mate on move 30: the bishop checks along the long diagonal, the knight closes h7, and your king g7 and g8. Twenty moves of the fifty-move rule were left.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.1: Attack demonstration: the bishop is light-squared, and the black king is on h8, the dark corner, the wrong one. The stage is Delétang's triangles: the same plan as in the a8 example.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.2: Check on f7: the knight drives the black king out of h8. With your king on g6, it only has g8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.3: Forced: the black king goes to g8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.4: Your king goes to f6 and protects the knight. The knight covers h8, and the bishop h7: the black king only has f8, towards a8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.5: Forced: the black king goes to f8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.6: The bishop goes to h7 and closes g8: the black king cannot go back to the wrong corner and only has e8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.7: Forced: the black king goes to e8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.8: The knight goes to e5 and covers d7 and f7. The black king stays on the edge, with d8 and f8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoErrado.9: The black king goes to d8, away from your king. It has left the wrong corner, and Delétang's triangles now take it towards a8.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.1: Attack demonstration: here the bishop is light-squared, and the black king is already next to h1, the corner of the bishop's colour. The stage is the final net: there is nothing to push.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.2: The knight goes to f4 and closes g2 and h3. The black king only has g1 and h1.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.3: The black king goes to g1: outside the corner, it is the defence that delays mate the longest.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.4: Your king goes to g3 and closes f2, g2 and h2. The bishop covers f1: the black king only has h1 left.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.5: Forced: the black king goes to h1.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.6: The bishop goes to e2 and covers f1. The black king only has g1.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.7: Forced: the black king goes to g1.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.8: Check on h3: the knight pushes the black king back to h1.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.9: Forced: the black king goes back to h1.
rot.convert.demos.cantoCerto.10: Mate in five moves: the bishop checks along the long diagonal, the knight closes g1, and your king g2 and h2.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.1: Attack demonstration: the stage of Delétang's triangles, with a light-squared bishop and the black king near h1. It is move 61, with 40 moves without a capture: mate must come by move 70.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.2: The bishop goes to e4 and closes g2 along the long diagonal; your king closes g3 and g4. The black king only has h2 and h4.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.3: The black king goes to h2, away from your king.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.4: The knight goes to d4, heading for e2 and f3, near the corner. The black king only has g1 and h3.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.5: The black king goes to g1, the defence that delays mate the longest.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.6: Your king goes to f3 and closes f2 and g2. The black king only has f1, h1 and h2.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.7: The black king goes to f1 and looks for a way out along the first rank.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.8: The knight goes to c2 and closes e1. The black king only has g1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.9: Forced: the black king goes to g1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.10: The knight goes to e3 and closes f1 and g2: the black king only has h1 and h2, and the final net begins.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.11: The black king goes to h1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.12: The bishop goes to f5 and covers h3. The black king only has g1 and h2.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.13: The black king goes to g1, outside the corner.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.14: Your king goes to g3 and closes f2, g2 and h2. The black king only has h1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.15: Forced: the black king goes to h1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.16: Your king goes to f2 and closes g1 and g2. The black king only has h2.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.17: Forced: the black king goes to h2.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.18: Check on f1: the knight sends the black king back, and the bishop on f5 covers h3. It only has h1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.19: Forced: the black king goes to h1.
rot.convert.demos.relogio.20: Mate on move 70, the last one before the limit: the bishop checks along the long diagonal, your king closes g1 and g2, and the knight h2.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.p: Attack: play White and give mate within 40 moves. The black king is next to the wrong corner: recognise the stage and lead it to the corner of the bishop's colour.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.fim: Mate: from the wrong corner to the corner of the bishop's colour, and then the final net.
rot.convert.pratica.fins.afogado: Stalemate: a draw. In the final net, close the black king's last square only with a move that gives check.
rot.convert.pratica.fins.repeticao: The position repeated three times: draw. At every move, recognise the stage and make progress in it, without going back.
rot.convert.pratica.fins.limite: The move limit ran out before mate. Lead the black king to the corner of the bishop's colour without detours: in a real game, the fifty-move rule leaves no margin either.
rot.convert.pratica.fins.insuficiente: A piece was captured, and the material is not enough to mate. Keep the bishop and the knight protected.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e3d2.1: Your king walks away and leaves the knight unprotected: the black king captures it, and the material is not enough to mate.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e3d2.2: Keep the knight next to your king, protected.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e3d3.1: Your king walks away and leaves the knight unprotected: the black king captures it, and the material is not enough to mate.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e3d3.2: Keep the knight next to your king, protected.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e3d4.1: Your king walks away and leaves the knight unprotected: the black king captures it, and the material is not enough to mate.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e3d4.2: Keep the knight next to your king, protected.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.f3g1.1: The knight goes to a square next to the black king, unprotected: it captures it, and the material is not enough to mate.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.f3g1.2: Keep the knight out of the black king's reach, or protected.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.f3h2.1: The knight goes to a square next to the black king, unprotected: it captures it, and the material is not enough to mate.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.f3h2.2: Keep the knight out of the black king's reach, or protected.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e1g3.1: The bishop goes to a square next to the black king, unprotected: it captures it, and the material is not enough to mate.
rot.convert.pratica.canto.err.e1g3.2: Keep the bishop out of the black king's reach, or protected.
rot.convert.pratica.inteira.p: Attack: the whole game, within the fifty-move rule. Barrier, Delétang's triangles and final net: at every move, recognise the stage.
rot.convert.pratica.inteira.fim: End of the chapter: from the centre to mate, stage by stage, within the fifty-move rule.
